name: Agabus
overview: Agabus is a male prophet from Jerusalem mentioned in the book of Acts. His role as a prophet identifies him as a divinely inspired spokesperson within the early Christian community. Beyond this, Scripture does not provide additional personal details or tribal affiliation.
namesAndTitles: The name Agabus appears only once in the biblical record and carries no specific meaning or divine origin noted in the text. It is simply recognized as his proper name.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Agabus beyond his identity as a prophet from Jerusalem. No other relational details are provided.
scriptureSignificance: Agabus is significant in the New Testament as a prophetic figure who served the early church in Jerusalem. His role underscores the ongoing work of the Holy Spirit in guiding and warning the Christian community during the formative years of the church. As a prophet, Agabus demonstrates the continuity of God’s revelation through chosen individuals in the early Christian era.
